scenes.heading: When homeostasis fails
scenes.sub: Find the broken link in the chain
scenes.say: Homeostasis only works if every part of the pathway does its job. So what happens when one part breaks?

scenes.heading: Which part has failed?
points: Gland: too little or too much hormone
scenes.say: Picture the stimulus response pathway as a chain, and ask which link snapped. Maybe the receptor misses the change. Maybe the gland makes too little or too much hormone. Maybe target cells don't respond. Or feedback stops working.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Group chat fails: the sender is kicked out, or everyone has it muted
scenes.science: Type 1: no insulin made. Type 2: cells respond poorly to insulin
scenes.breaks: A muted chat can be unmuted with one tap. Insulin resistance develops gradually and is managed, not switched off.
scenes.say: Think of the pancreas messaging a group chat: take in glucose! In type 1 diabetes, the sender has been kicked out: beta cells are destroyed, so no insulin is sent. In type 2, the message is sent, but most of the group has muted the chat. That's insulin resistance.

scenes.heading: Type 1 diabetes, step by step
steps: Little or no insulin: glucose stays high
scenes.say: Type 1 diabetes is autoimmune. The immune system destroys the beta cells, so little or no insulin is made, and blood glucose stays high. The kidneys can't reabsorb it all, so glucose ends up in the urine, taking water with it. The person makes lots of urine, feels thirsty and loses weight.

scenes.heading: Graves' disease
points: Fast heart, weight loss, feeling hot
scenes.say: Normally, high thyroxine switches off TSH. In Graves' disease, antibodies bind to the TSH receptors and keep switching the thyroid on, like a doorbell jammed on. TSH falls, but thyroxine stays high. Metabolism speeds up: fast heart, weight loss, feeling hot.

scenes.heading: Find the fault
scenes.question: Two patients have high blood glucose. Patient X has very low insulin. Patient Y has high insulin. Where is each fault?
lines: X: no insulin, so the gland has failed
Y: insulin made, but cells don't respond
Answer: X = gland fault, Y = target cells
scenes.say: Patient X and patient Y both have high blood glucose. X has very low insulin, so the gland has failed. That fits type 1. Y has high insulin, but glucose is still high, so the target cells aren't responding. That fits type 2. Low hormone: check the gland. High hormone: check the target cells.

scenes.heading: Two kinds of diabetes
scenes.say: Mellitus means honey: it's about glucose and insulin. Insipidus means tasteless: it's about ADH and water. Too little ADH, or kidneys that ignore it, means lots of dilute urine.

points: Find the broken link in the pathway
Type 1: no insulin; type 2: poor response
scenes.say: Quick recap. Find the broken link. Type 1 diabetes means no insulin; type 2 means cells respond poorly. In Graves' disease, antibodies ignore feedback. Diabetes insipidus is an ADH fault. Now try the practice questions!
